*[[Babysit Your Very Hard to Handle Sister|How to Babysit Your Very Hard to Handle Sister]]
*[[Babysit a 1 Year Old Girl All Day and Night|How to Babysit a 1 Year Old Girl All Day and Night]]

added:
#[[Prepare for a Babysitting Job|Prepare for the job]]. It's really fun to babysit but it's also hard.[Keep a Calendar to make sure you are available when asked to babysit. This will help avoid the frustration of a last minute change of plans due to poor planning. Find out what time you will be needed, night or day, and again check to make sure you are available. If not, you can ask the person if you can babysit another time, or babysit another child. All of us can't babysit at the right time, whether you go to school, whether working, whether busy or you have a kid to take care of yourself.

[[Image:Babysit Step 1.jpg|center|550px]]

#  Write down the following information: [Call Someone on a Cell Phone number]  the address and the phone number of the place where they will be, and the child's name, blood type, doctor's name, doctor's number, and allergies. These are very important in an emergency. You have to know these because you never know what will happen. You technically need most of the kid/baby's medical information. Also ask where the first aid things are kept.

[[Image:Babysit Step 2.jpg|center|550px]]

#  Make sure they give you ''all'' of the [[Be Prepared for Any Kind of Emergency (for Kids)|emergency]] phone numbers needed. Police, ambulance, fire department and their cell phone numbers are very important, and should be written clearly on the refrigerator. If they give you a grandparent's phone number that’s also good, because the parents might be at a concert or somewhere loud and may not be able to hear their cell phone. Some other good people can be people the parents really know, and very good friends that you know well.

[[Image:Babysit Step 3.jpg|center|550px]]

#  Make sure the parents give you instructions if caring for an [[Babysit an Infant|infant]]. Write down any and all instructions. It is better if the parents write it down because you could make a mistake when writing. This is yet another very important thing to do. Find out where all the gear, such as baby bottles or spare clothes, are kept.

[[Image:Babysit Step 4.jpg|center|550px]]

#  Always make sure your the right age to do this big step. You should be '''at least''' 13  years old when you first start babysitting. Under that age, it might prove to be too much responsibility.

[[Image:Babysit Step 5.jpg|center|550px]]

#  Ask in advance if you can do certain things such as cook, use the computer, use the TV, use the phone, etc. The parents may want to keep the lines clear in case they want to call.

[[Image:Babysit Step 6.jpg|center|550px]]

#Make sure to find out any special household rules or off limits areas. Ask if they are expecting anyone or if you should [[Answer the Telephone When You're Babysitting|answer the phone]]. Better yet, let the answering machine take messages, this way you won't become nervous or distracted. You need to keep your eyes on the baby. No answering machine? Ask the parents to get one, or you can forward it to your cell phone so you can just grab it out of your pocket. Make sure the caller ID shows up, and don't pick up for a stranger. Ask the parents of phone numbers you can approve, and say that the parents aren't available, without telling them you're alone.

[[Image:Babysit Step 7.jpg|center|550px]]

#  Never [[Answer the Door Safely|answer the door]] unless you are expecting someone and only when you make sure that it is that person. Peek out of the peephole or window (do not open the door) first before answering the door. The person at the door may be a stranger. Also ask the parents for a list of people they know, and ask to describe them on the piece of paper.

[[Image:Babysit Step 8.jpg|center|550px]]

#  [[Entertain Kids When You Are Babysitting|Have a structured idea of what you're going to do]] while you're babysitting. Make puppets with the children out of paper bags and have coloring books they like and crayons with you. Play their favorite activity, and do whatever they ask you to do as long as they are safe. [[Stay Safe at Night|Being safe]] is the most important task you can do when you are babysitting. You must keep the child happy especially if it's young. The parents can insult you for making the child sad. It always helps if you stay in a positive, up-beat attitude when you are watching children.

[[Image:Babysit Step 9.jpg|center|550px]]

#  Never leave them out of your sight!'''Keep the children you're watching in one area''', so that you can make sure everyone's safe. If there are older children you are watching, keep them limited to the house, or if you're outside, to the backyard. Smaller children should stay where you can see them at all times. All children should be kept as far away from a street as possible.

[[Image:Babysit Step 10.jpg|center|550px]]

#  [[Put a Babysitting Charge to Sleep|Put the children to bed]] at the time the parent wants them in bed. Don't let them fall asleep early or stay up late. If they go to bed early, they may wake up later and not go back to sleep! Put the children to sleep like they are always put to bed. If one of the children cry, or throw a fit, try to give them their favorite cuddly toy, or sippy cup/bottle. Especially with slightly older children who want to stay up to carry on playing, make them aware of the fact that there will be no more playing or fun anyway if they try staying up on purpose for you will not join in nor give them their games. If the child still cries for no reason this probably is because the child is tired. He/She will eventually fall asleep. Throughout the night check up on the children however many times you think is necessary.

[[Image:Babysit Step 11.jpg|center|550px]]

#  [[Clean Fast|Clean up]] before the parents get home and while the children are sleeping. Pick up toys and dishes. Make it look like you were never there and the parents will greatly appreciate it, because nobody wants to come home to a dirty home.

[[Image:Babysit Step 12.jpg|center|550px]]

#  [[Play With Kids While Babysitting|Play with the kids]]! Kids love it when you play with them! Don't be afraid to go outside and get your hands dirty! Then fights and/or disagreements are less likely to pop up. Also the kids have an image of a fun, caring, trustworthy babysitter in their minds! Remember kids report how much they liked the babysitter and if they go on and on about how fun you were, you might get invited back! Just don't be afraid to let your inner child come out, the kids love it. Also don't forget that kids always love it when played with.

[[Image:Babysit Step 13.jpg|center|550px]]

# Research ahead of time. What do the kids like? depending on their age, they will likely have different interests.

[[Image:Babysit Step 14.jpg|center|550px]]

#  Become a certified babysitter. Look up classes to take. You will learn many new things and will be more trustworthy when it comes to babysitting an infant.

[[Image:Babysit Step 15.jpg|center|550px]]

added: *Try to make the least amount of noise as possible so they won't wake up until their parents get home.

* If a little kid is having a bath play with them with bath toys and don't let them get out of your sight to prevent them drowning.

*Kids like stories, and they'll be impressed by even the worst storytellers. Come equipped with obscure fairy tales they probably haven't heard, like "The Shoemaker and the Elves" or "The Twelve Dancing Princesses." When you can't get them to go to sleep or eat their food, make a deal that if they do what they're supposed to, you'll tell them a story. Make sure you edit out anything that might be scary or disturbing, because Grimm's tales can be kind of creepy sometimes.
*If the child is known to move a lot then ask the parents to bring out a play-pen, If they don't have one then put all of the children into one room with the cot and put on an appropriate film.
* Have fun! Don't be afraid to let your inner child out!
*You might want to take a class first because parents would rather hire someone who knows what they are doing. Even better, give the parents references when you first meet them.
*If you are able to, keep the child's information so you don't have to write it down every time. Just make sure you don't forget it next time.
* Make sure to watch your language! You don't want the kids hearing you say it thinking it's okay and have them repeat it to their parents.

*When you are changing a baby's diaper on a changing table or counter, make sure that you have everything (baby wipes, diapers, baby powder, etc.) within reach so that you won't have to walk away to get anything. Don't leave the child for even a second, because in that second they could roll off of the table. Even if the table has sides, they could hurt themselves. So stay with the child the entire time, and get the child off of the table as soon as possible.
*Be nice to the kids and don't get in their face, that will scare them away but if you are family the case may be different and they may know you enough to not be scared of you.
*Get a movie that you would like to see (make sure it's appropriate for the kids) and watch it when they fall asleep.

*If the children will not go to sleep then put on a film that is appropriate(not a cartoon and not a musical)this will make them bored and make them sleep more,however,if that doesn't work then make them a hot drink but add cold water (1/3)this will also make them sleepy.
* Have patience. Kids might not always obey you the first time, but remember to remain calm!
*Don't give kids anything packed with sugar even if they cry for it, unless the treat is approved by the parents.
*Don't let them jump on the furniture.
*If you are babysitting an infant, only feed them things the size of their fist or smaller.
*Don't ever leave the kids with strangers, even if the kids seem to know them.
*You probably shouldn't believe the kid if they say something along the lines of "Mommy lets me do this/that" because they're probably lying.
*Follow the rules given to you by the parent. If you disobey them, they probably will not invite you back.

added: [[Image:65969524_07c888ab7a.jpg|200px|right]]Babysitting a young child, whether it is a sibling or the neighbor next door, requires some training, patience and understanding of how to calm a child/baby or help and comfort them in case of need of any help of a poopy diaper or a mess that the baby makes while eating. Also if the child might have allergies.
[[Category:Babysitting]]
== Steps ==

#[[Prepare for a Babysitting Job|Prepare for the job]]. It's really fun to babysit but it's also hard.[Keep a Calendar to make sure you are available when asked to babysit. This will help avoid the frustration of a last minute change of plans due to poor planning. Find out what time you will be needed, night or day, and again check to make sure you are available. If not, you can ask the person if you can babysit another time, or babysit another child. All of us can't babysit at the right time, whether you go to school, whether working, whether busy or you have a kid to take care of yourself.

#  Write down the following information: [Call Someone on a Cell Phone cell phone number]  the address and the phone number of the place where they will be, and the child's name, blood type, doctor's name, doctor's number, and allergies. These are very important in an emergency. You have to know these because you never know what will happen. You technically need most of the kid/baby's medical information. Also ask where the first aid things are kept.

#  Make sure they give you ''all'' of the [[Be Prepared for Any Kind of Emergency (for Kids)|emergency]] phone numbers needed. Police, ambulance, fire department and their cell phone numbers are very important, and should be written clearly on the refrigerator. If they give you a grandparent's phone number that’s also good, because the parents might be at a concert or somewhere loud and may not be able to hear their cell phone. Some other good people can be people the parents really know, and very good friends that you know well.

#  Make sure the parents give you instructions if caring for an [[Babysit an Infant|infant]]. Write down any and all instructions. It is better if the parents write it down because you could make a mistake when writing. This is yet another very important thing to do. Find out where all the gear, such as baby bottles or spare clothes, are kept.
#  Always make sure your the right age to do this big step. You should be '''at least''' 13  years old when you first start babysitting. Under that age, it might prove to be too much responsibility.
#  Ask in advance if you can do certain things such as cook, use the computer, use the TV, use the phone, etc. The parents may want to keep the lines clear in case they want to call.

#Make sure to find out any special household rules or off limits areas. Ask if they are expecting anyone or if you should [[Answer the Telephone When You're Babysitting|answer the phone]]. Better yet, let the answering machine take messages, this way you won't become nervous or distracted. You need to keep your eyes on the baby. No answering machine? Ask the parents to get one, or you can forward it to your cell phone so you can just grab it out of your pocket. Make sure the caller ID shows up, and don't pick up for a stranger. Ask the parents of phone numbers you can approve, and say that the parents aren't available, without telling them you're alone.

#  Never [[Answer the Door Safely|answer the door]] unless you are expecting someone and only when you make sure that it is that person. Peek out of the peephole or window (do not open the door) first before answering the door. The person at the door may be a stranger. Also ask the parents for a list of people they know, and ask to describe them on the piece of paper.

#  [[Entertain Kids When You Are Babysitting|Have a structured idea of what you're going to do]] while you're babysitting. Make puppets with the children out of paper bags and have coloring books they like and crayons with you. Play their favorite activity, and do whatever they ask you to do as long as they are safe. [[Stay Safe at Night|Being safe]] is the most important task you can do when you are babysitting. You must keep the child happy especially if it's young. The parents can insult you for making the child sad. It always helps if you stay in a positive, up-beat attitude when you are watching children.

#  Never leave them out of your sight!'''Keep the children you're watching in one area''', so that you can make sure everyone's safe. If there are older children you are watching, keep them limited to the house, or if you're outside, to the backyard. Smaller children should stay where you can see them at all times. All children should be kept as far away from a street as possible.

#  [[Put a Babysitting Charge to Sleep|Put the children to bed]] at the time the parent wants them in bed. Don't let them fall asleep early or stay up late. If they go to bed early, they may wake up later and not go back to sleep! Put the children to sleep like they are always put to bed. If one of the children cry, or throw a fit, try to give them their favorite cuddly toy, or sippy cup/bottle. Especially with slightly older children who want to stay up to carry on playing, make them aware of the fact that there will be no more playing or fun anyway if they try staying up on purpose for you will not join in nor give them their games. If the child still cries for no reason this probably is because the child is tired. He/She will eventually fall asleep. Throughout the night check up on the children however many times you think is necessary.

#  [[Clean Fast|Clean up]] before the parents get home and while the children are sleeping. Pick up toys and dishes. Make it look like you were never there and the parents will greatly appreciate it, because nobody wants to come home to a dirty home.

#  [[Play With Kids While Babysitting|Play with the kids]]! Kids love it when you play with them! Don't be afraid to go outside and get your hands dirty! Then fights and/or disagreements are less likely to pop up. Also the kids have an image of a fun, caring, trustworthy babysitter in their minds! Remember kids report how much they liked the babysitter and if they go on and on about how fun you were, you might get invited back! Just don't be afraid to let your inner child come out, the kids love it. Also don't forget that kids always love it when played with.
# Research ahead of time. What do the kids like? depending on their age, they will likely have different interests.
#  Become a certified babysitter. Look up classes to take. You will learn many new things and will be more trustworthy when it comes to babysitting an infant.
== Video ==
{{Video:Babysit|}}
== Tips ==

*A lot of children are scared of monsters at night. If you have trouble with the children, tell them, "I know a secret. It always works with me. It's a secret word that makes all monsters go away." Then suggest that the children say something like Winnie The Pooh is going to take care of you, or something that sounds funny. Say, "Let's say it together." Say it with the child, then offer to check in their closet, under their bed, behind curtains, and any other place a monster may be hiding. Be sure to tell the child before you leave that you've checked and there are no monsters in their room, but the secret word will make all monsters stay away for good now.
*If you're giving a child a bath, don't leave him/her alone for even two seconds. Make sure that you have all necessary bathing equipment in the bathroom before you put the child in the bathtub.

*Kids like stories, and they'll be impressed by even the worst storytellers. Come equipped with obscure fairy tales they probably haven't heard, like "The Shoemaker and the Elves" or "The Twelve Dancing Princesses." When you can't get them to go to sleep or eat their food, make a deal that if they do what they're supposed to, you'll tell them a story. Make sure you edit out anything that might be scary or disturbing, because Grimm's tales can be kind of creepy sometimes.
*Try to make the least amount of noise as possible so they won't wake up until their parents get home.
*If the child is known to move a lot then ask the parents to bring out a play-pen, If they don't have one then put all of the children into one room with the cot and put on an appropriate film.

*Always change the toddler or infant's diaper when instructed to. If you are not given a specific time, change the diaper before naps and after. Most of the time you will know when it is time to change it, as it is very smelly.
*Find a cookbook and make no-bake cookies if you can't use the oven.Yum Yum
*Always feel free to call the parents if you feel you need to. They will usually always leave a couple of phone numbers for you to call.
* If there is an emergency than call 911 before calling the parents because you made need the police/fire department/ambulance to be there immediately.
* If a little kid is having a bath play with them with bath toys and don't let them get out of your sight to prevent them drowning.

*When you are changing a baby's diaper on a changing table or counter, make sure that you have everything (baby wipes, diapers, baby powder, etc.) within reach so that you won't have to walk away to get anything. Don't leave the child for even a second, because in that second they could roll off of the table. Even if the table has sides, they could hurt themselves. So stay with the child the entire time, and get the child off of the table as soon as possible.
* Have fun! Don't be afraid to let your inner child out!
* Don't yell at the kids! The parents could get very upset and you wouldn't have a job.
* Make sure to watch your language! You don't want the kids hearing you say it thinking it's okay and have them repeat it to their parents.
*If you are able to, keep the child's information so you don't have to write it down every time. Just make sure you don't forget it next time.

*If the children will not go to sleep then put on a film that is appropriate(not a cartoon and not a musical)this will make them bored and make them sleep more,however,if that doesn't work then make them a hot drink but add cold water (1/3)this will also make them sleepy.
*The kids you're babysitting won't fall asleep at the same time, so ask the ones who are not asleep to color with you (or find a quiet activity to engage in).
*Never invite your friends or anyone over without the parent's permission.
*You might want to take a class first because parents would rather hire someone who knows what they are doing. Even better, give the parents references when you first meet them.

*To make the children behave more then make sticker chart before you arrive at the house. when you are at the house tell the children that when they get a certain amount of stars they will be rewarded with a biscuit or a sweet.
*Be nice to the kids and don't get in their face, that will scare them away but if you are family the case may be different and they may know you enough to not be scared of you.
*Get a movie that you would like to see (make sure it's appropriate for the kids) and watch it when they fall asleep.
*If you are watching a young child, and there are dogs, keep the child away from the dog. If at all possible, keep the dog in a separate room or outside.
* Have patience. Kids might not always obey you the first time, but remember to remain calm!
== Warnings ==

*When putting a baby to bed, '''do not''' lay it on its belly. Your baby can get Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS) if you do that. Do not prop a baby up with pillows, as these may cause it to suffocate.
*You probably shouldn't believe the kid if they say something along the lines of "Mommy lets me do this/that" because they're probably lying.
*If you are babysitting an infant, only feed them things the size of their fist or smaller.
*Don't let them jump on the furniture.
*Never fall asleep when babysitting. It's never a good idea to fall asleep on the job, especially if the kids that you're baby-sitting for could get into mischief and trouble.
*Don't ever leave the kids with strangers, even if the kids seem to know them.
*Be VERY careful around animals, no matter how nice they seem.

*Kid-proof the areas you will be playing in. Make sure all electrical outlets are covered and put all sharp objects away. Make sure you do not let the kids get near cleaning fluids. Keep all types of medicines away, the child could think it is candy and gobble them up. Close all windows. If you're watching a toddler, keep all doors leading to basement stairs closed, and all bathroom doors closed.
*Don't give kids anything packed with sugar even if they cry for it, unless the treat is approved by the parents.
*Never let toddlers walk up or down stairs without you with them.
*'''Always''' keep an eye on the children you are babysitting, because they might get hurt when you are not looking. Never let small children out of your sight.
*Follow the rules given to you by the parent. If you disobey them, they probably will not invite you back.
== Things You will Need ==
*Crafts
*Notepad for messages
*Bag or Tote
*Coloring pages
*Books
*Crayons/Pencils/Markers
*Games
*A fun and parent approved video for them to watch
*Emergency information
*Small snacks for you and the kids (Be cautious of any food allergies.)
*Clean diapers
*Page for scavenger hunt
*A pen to write the stuff with
*A booster seat if traveling (if they need it)
*A stroller (if going to walk around the park and are small children)
*Transport if you are taking to movies or into town
*Rewards for a good job (cookies or pencils will do)
*References (optional)
*First aid kit
*Cell phone (if you have one)
*Hand sanitizer
*Back up clothes
*Contact infarmation

*If the children will not go to sleep then put on a film that is appropriate(not a cartoon and not a musical)this will make them bored and make them sleep more,however,if that doesn't work then make them a hot drink but add cold water (1/3)this will also make them sleepy.
*The kids you're babysitting won't fall asleep at the same time, so ask the ones who are not asleep to color with you (or find a quiet activity to engage in).
*Never invite your friends or anyone over without the parent's permission.
*You might want to take a class first because parents would rather hire someone who knows what they are doing. Even better, give the parents references when you first meet them.

*To make the children behave more then make sticker chart before you arrive at the house. when you are at the house tell the children that when they get a certain amount of stars they will be rewarded with a biscuit or a sweet.
*Be nice to the kids and don't get in their face, that will scare them away but if you are family the case may be different and they may know you enough to not be scared of you.
*Get a movie that you would like to see (make sure it's appropriate for the kids) and watch it when they fall asleep.
*If you are watching a young child, and there are dogs, keep the child away from the dog. If at all possible, keep the dog in a separate room or outside.
* Have patience. Kids might not always obey you the first time, but remember to remain calm!
== Warnings ==

*When putting a baby to bed, '''do not''' lay it on its belly. Your baby can get Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS) if you do that. Do not prop a baby up with pillows, as these may cause it to suffocate.
*You probably shouldn't believe the kid if they say something along the lines of "Mommy lets me do this/that" because they're probably lying.
*If you are babysitting an infant, only feed them things the size of their fist or smaller.
*Don't let them jump on the furniture.
*Never fall asleep when babysitting. It's never a good idea to fall asleep on the job, especially if the kids that you're baby-sitting for could get into mischief and trouble.
*Don't ever leave the kids with strangers, even if the kids seem to know them.
*Be VERY careful around animals, no matter how nice they seem.

*Kid-proof the areas you will be playing in. Make sure all electrical outlets are covered and put all sharp objects away. Make sure you do not let the kids get near cleaning fluids. Keep all types of medicines away, the child could think it is candy and gobble them up. Close all windows. If you're watching a toddler, keep all doors leading to basement stairs closed, and all bathroom doors closed.
*Don't give kids anything packed with sugar even if they cry for it, unless the treat is approved by the parents.
*Never let toddlers walk up or down stairs without you with them.
*'''Always''' keep an eye on the children you are babysitting, because they might get hurt when you are not looking. Never let small children out of your sight.
*Follow the rules given to you by the parent. If you disobey them, they probably will not invite you back.

*Crafts
*Notepad for messages
*Bag or Tote
*Coloring pages
*Books
*Crayons/Pencils/Markers
*Games
*A fun and parent approved video for them to watch
*Emergency information
*Small snacks for you and the kids (Be cautious of any food allergies.)
*Clean diapers
*Page for scavenger hunt
*A pen to write the stuff with
*A booster seat if traveling (if they need it)
*A stroller (if going to walk around the park and are small children)
*Transport if you are taking to movies or into town
*Rewards for a good job (cookies or pencils will do)
*References (optional)
*First aid kit
*Cell phone (if you have one)
*Hand sanitizer
*Back up clothes
*Contact infarmation

added: * Have fun! Don't be afraid to let your inner child out!

*Kids like stories, and they'll be impressed by even the worst storytellers. Come equipped with obscure fairy tales they probably haven't heard, like "The Shoemaker and the Elves" or "The Twelve Dancing Princesses." When you can't get them to go to sleep or eat their food, make a deal that if they do what they're supposed to, you'll tell them a story. Make sure you edit out anything that might be scary or disturbing, because Grimm's tales can be kind of creepy sometimes.
* Have patience. Kids might not always obey you the first time, but remember to remain calm!
* If there is an emergency than call 911 before calling the parents because you made need the police/fire department/ambulance to be there immediately.

*If the children will not go to sleep then put on a film that is appropriate(not a cartoon and not a musical)this will make them bored and make them sleep more,however,if that doesn't work then make them a hot drink but add cold water (1/3)this will also make them sleepy.
*Find a cookbook and make no-bake cookies if you can't use the oven.Yum Yum
*If you are able to, keep the child's information so you don't have to write it down every time. Just make sure you don't forget it next time.
*Try to make the least amount of noise as possible so they won't wake up until their parents get home.
*If you are watching a young child, and there are dogs, keep the child away from the dog. If at all possible, keep the dog in a separate room or outside.
*Be nice to the kids and don't get in their face, that will scare them away but if you are family the case may be different and they may know you enough to not be scared of you.

*A lot of children are scared of monsters at night. If you have trouble with the children, tell them, "I know a secret. It always works with me. It's a secret word that makes all monsters go away." Then suggest that the children say something like Winnie The Pooh is going to take care of you, or something that sounds funny. Say, "Let's say it together." Say it with the child, then offer to check in their closet, under their bed, behind curtains, and any other place a monster may be hiding. Be sure to tell the child before you leave that you've checked and there are no monsters in their room, but the secret word will make all monsters stay away for good now.
*You might want to take a class first because parents would rather hire someone who knows what they are doing. Even better, give the parents references when you first meet them.

*To make the children behave more then make sticker chart before you arrive at the house. when you are at the house tell the children that when they get a certain amount of stars they will be rewarded with a biscuit or a sweet.
*'''Always''' keep an eye on the children you are babysitting, because they might get hurt when you are not looking. Never let small children out of your sight.
*Never fall asleep when babysitting. It's never a good idea to fall asleep on the job, especially if the kids that you're baby-sitting for could get into mischief and trouble.
*Don't ever leave the kids with strangers, even if the kids seem to know them.
*Never let toddlers walk up or down stairs without you with them.
*Don't let them jump on the furniture.

added: #  Make sure they give you ''all'' of the [[Be Prepared for Any Kind of Emergency (for Kids)|emergency]] phone numbers needed. Police, ambulance, fire department and their cell phone numbers are very important, and should be written clearly on the refrigerator. If they give you a grandparent's phone number that’s also good, because the parents might be at a concert or somewhere loud and may not be able to hear their cell phone. Some other good people can be people the parents really know, and very good friends that you know well.

*You probably shouldn't believe the kid if they say something along the lines of "Mommy lets me do this/that" because they're probably lying.

*Be VERY careful around animals, no matter how nice they seem.

*If you're giving a child a bath, don't leave him/her alone for even two seconds. Make sure that you have all necessary bathing equipment in the bathroom before you put the child in the bathtub.
* If a little kid is having a bath play with them with bath toys and don't let them get out of your sight to prevent them drowning.
* If there is an emergency than call 911 before calling the parents because you made need the police/fire department/ambulance to be there immediately.
*Find a cookbook and make no-bake cookies if you can't use the oven.Yum Yum
*If you are able to, keep the child's information so you don't have to write it down every time. Just make sure you don't forget it next time.

*When you are changing a baby's diaper on a changing table or counter, make sure that you have everything (baby wipes, diapers, baby powder, etc.) within reach so that you won't have to walk away to get anything. Don't leave the child for even a second, because in that second they could roll off of the table. Even if the table has sides, they could hurt themselves. So stay with the child the entire time, and get the child off of the table as soon as possible.

*A lot of children are scared of monsters at night. If you have trouble with the children, tell them, "I know a secret. It always works with me. It's a secret word that makes all monsters go away." Then suggest that the children say something like Winnie The Pooh is going to take care of you, or something that sounds funny. Say, "Let's say it together." Say it with the child, then offer to check in their closet, under their bed, behind curtains, and any other place a monster may be hiding. Be sure to tell the child before you leave that you've checked and there are no monsters in their room, but the secret word will make all monsters stay away for good now.

*Always change the toddler or infant's diaper when instructed to. If you are not given a specific time, change the diaper before naps and after. Most of the time you will know when it is time to change it, as it is very smelly.
*Always feel free to call the parents if you feel you need to. They will usually always leave a couple of phone numbers for you to call.
*The kids you're babysitting won't fall asleep at the same time, so ask the ones who are not asleep to color with you (or find a quiet activity to engage in).
*You might want to take a class first because parents would rather hire someone who knows what they are doing. Even better, give the parents references when you first meet them.
*Get a movie that you would like to see (make sure it's appropriate for the kids) and watch it when they fall asleep.
*Follow the rules given to you by the parent. If you disobey them, they probably will not invite you back.
*'''Always''' keep an eye on the children you are babysitting, because they might get hurt when you are not looking. Never let small children out of your sight.

*When putting a baby to bed, '''do not''' lay it on its belly. Your baby can get Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS) if you do that. Do not prop a baby up with pillows, as these may cause it to suffocate.
*If you are babysitting an infant, only feed them things the size of their fist or smaller.
*Never fall asleep when babysitting. It's never a good idea to fall asleep on the job, especially if the kids that you're baby-sitting for could get into mischief and trouble.
*Never let toddlers walk up or down stairs without you with them.
*Don't give kids anything packed with sugar even if they cry for it, unless the treat is approved by the parents.
*Be VERY careful around animals, no matter how nice they seem.

added: [[Image:65969524_07c888ab7a.jpg|200px|right]]Babysitting a young child, whether it is a sibling or the neighbor next door, requires some training, patience and understanding of how to calm a child/baby or help and comfort them in case of need of any help of a poopy diaper or a mess that the baby makes while eating. Also if the child might have allergies.
[[Category:Babysitting]]
== Steps ==

#[[Prepare for a Babysitting Job|Prepare for the job]]. It's really fun to babysit but it's also hard.[Keep a Calendar to make sure you are available when asked to babysit. This will help avoid the frustration of a last minute change of plans due to poor planning. Find out what time you will be needed, night or day, and again check to make sure you are available. If not, you can ask the person if you can babysit another time, or babysit another child. All of us can't babysit at the right time, whether you go to school, whether working, whether busy or you have a kid to take care of yourself.

#  Write down the following information: [Call Someone on a Cell Phone cell phone number]  the address and the phone number of the place where they will be, and the child's name, blood type, doctor's name, doctor's number, and allergies. These are very important in an emergency. You have to know these because you never know what will happen. You technically need most of the kid/baby's medical information. Also ask where the first aid things are kept.

#  Make sure they give you ''all'' of the [[Be Prepared for Any Kind of Emergency (for Kids)|emergency]] phone numbers needed. Police, ambulance, fire department and their cell phone numbers are very important, and should be written clearly on the refrigerator. If they give you a grandparent's phone number that’s also good, because the parents might be at a concert or somewhere loud and may not be able to hear their cell phone. Some other good people can be people the parents really know, and very good friends that you know well.

#  Make sure the parents give you instructions if caring for an [[Babysit an Infant|infant]]. Write down any and all instructions. It is better if the parents write it down because you could make a mistake when writing. This is yet another very important thing to do. Find out where all the gear, such as baby bottles or spare clothes, are kept.
#  Always make sure your the right age to do this big step. You should be '''at least''' 13  years old when you first start babysitting. Under that age, it might prove to be too much responsibility.
#  Ask in advance if you can do certain things such as cook, use the computer, use the TV, use the phone, etc. The parents may want to keep the lines clear in case they want to call.

#Make sure to find out any special household rules or off limits areas. Ask if they are expecting anyone or if you should [[Answer the Telephone When You're Babysitting|answer the phone]]. Better yet, let the answering machine take messages, this way you won't become nervous or distracted. You need to keep your eyes on the baby. No answering machine? Ask the parents to get one, or you can forward it to your cell phone so you can just grab it out of your pocket. Make sure the caller ID shows up, and don't pick up for a stranger. Ask the parents of phone numbers you can approve, and say that the parents aren't available, without telling them you're alone.

#  Never [[Answer the Door Safely|answer the door]] unless you are expecting someone and only when you make sure that it is that person. Peek out of the peephole or window (do not open the door) first before answering the door. The person at the door may be a stranger. Also ask the parents for a list of people they know, and ask to describe them on the piece of paper.

#  [[Entertain Kids When You Are Babysitting|Have a structured idea of what you're going to do]] while you're babysitting. Make puppets with the children out of paper bags and have coloring books they like and crayons with you. Play their favorite activity, and do whatever they ask you to do as long as they are safe. [[Stay Safe at Night|Being safe]] is the most important task you can do when you are babysitting. You must keep the child happy especially if it's young. The parents can insult you for making the child sad. It always helps if you stay in a positive, up-beat attitude when you are watching children.

#  Never leave them out of your sight!'''Keep the children you're watching in one area''', so that you can make sure everyone's safe. If there are older children you are watching, keep them limited to the house, or if you're outside, to the backyard. Smaller children should stay where you can see them at all times. All children should be kept as far away from a street as possible.

#  [[Put a Babysitting Charge to Sleep|Put the children to bed]] at the time the parent wants them in bed. Don't let them fall asleep early or stay up late. If they go to bed early, they may wake up later and not go back to sleep! Put the children to sleep like they are always put to bed. If one of the children cry, or throw a fit, try to give them their favorite cuddly toy, or sippy cup/bottle. Especially with slightly older children who want to stay up to carry on playing, make them aware of the fact that there will be no more playing or fun anyway if they try staying up on purpose for you will not join in nor give them their games. If the child still cries for no reason this probably is because the child is tired. He/She will eventually fall asleep. Throughout the night check up on the children however many times you think is necessary.

#  [[Clean Fast|Clean up]] before the parents get home and while the children are sleeping. Pick up toys and dishes. Make it look like you were never there and the parents will greatly appreciate it, because nobody wants to come home to a dirty home.

#  [[Play With Kids While Babysitting|Play with the kids]]! Kids love it when you play with them! Don't be afraid to go outside and get your hands dirty! Then fights and/or disagreements are less likely to pop up. Also the kids have an image of a fun, caring, trustworthy babysitter in their minds! Remember kids report how much they liked the babysitter and if they go on and on about how fun you were, you might get invited back! Just don't be afraid to let your inner child come out, the kids love it. Also don't forget that kids always love it when played with.
# Research ahead of time. What do the kids like? depending on their age, they will likely have different interests.
#  Become a certified babysitter. Look up classes to take. You will learn many new things and will be more trustworthy when it comes to babysitting an infant.

*Always change the toddler or infant's diaper when instructed to. If you are not given a specific time, change the diaper before naps and after. Most of the time you will know when it is time to change it, as it is very smelly.

* Make sure to watch your language! You don't want the kids hearing you say it thinking it's okay and have them repeat it to their parents.

*Be VERY careful around animals, no matter how nice they seem.

*Kid-proof the areas you will be playing in. Make sure all electrical outlets are covered and put all sharp objects away. Make sure you do not let the kids get near cleaning fluids. Keep all types of medicines away, the child could think it is candy and gobble them up. Close all windows. *Don't give kids anything packed with sugar even if they cry for it, unless the treat is approved by the parents.
*Follow the rules given to you by the parent. If you disobey them, they probably will not invite you back.
*Don't let them jump on the furniture.
*Don't ever leave the kids with strangers, even if the kids seem to know them.
*You probably shouldn't believe the kid if they say something along the lines of "Mommy lets me do this/that" because they're probably lying.

== Steps ==

#[[Prepare for a Babysitting Job|Prepare for the job]]. It's really fun to babysit but it's also hard.[Keep a Calendar to make sure you are available when asked to babysit. This will help avoid the frustration of a last minute change of plans due to poor planning. Find out what time you will be needed, night or day, and again check to make sure you are available. If not, you can ask the person if you can babysit another time, or babysit another child. All of us can't babysit at the right time, whether you go to school, whether working, whether busy or you have a kid to take care of yourself.

#  Write down the following information: [Call Someone on a Cell Phone cell phone number]  the address and the phone number of the place where they will be, and the child's name, blood type, doctor's name, doctor's number, and allergies. These are very important in an emergency. You have to know these because you never know what will happen. You technically need most of the kid/baby's medical information. Also ask where the first aid things are kept.

#  Make sure they give you ''all'' of the [[Be Prepared for Any Kind of Emergency (for Kids)|emergency]] phone numbers needed. Police, ambulance, fire department and their cell phone numbers are very important, and should be written clearly on the refrigerator. If they give you a grandparent's phone number that’s also good, because the parents might be at a concert or somewhere loud and may not be able to hear their cell phone. Some other good people can be people the parents really know, and very good friends that you know well.

#  Make sure the parents give you instructions if caring for an [[Babysit an Infant|infant]]. Write down any and all instructions. It is better if the parents write it down because you could make a mistake when writing. This is yet another very important thing to do. Find out where all the gear, such as baby bottles or spare clothes, are kept.
#  Always make sure your the right age to do this big step. You should be '''at least''' 13  years old when you first start babysitting. Under that age, it might prove to be too much responsibility.
#  Ask in advance if you can do certain things such as cook, use the computer, use the TV, use the phone, etc. The parents may want to keep the lines clear in case they want to call.

#Make sure to find out any special household rules or off limits areas. Ask if they are expecting anyone or if you should [[Answer the Telephone When You're Babysitting|answer the phone]]. Better yet, let the answering machine take messages, this way you won't become nervous or distracted. You need to keep your eyes on the baby. No answering machine? Ask the parents to get one, or you can forward it to your cell phone so you can just grab it out of your pocket. Make sure the caller ID shows up, and don't pick up for a stranger. Ask the parents of phone numbers you can approve, and say that the parents aren't available, without telling them you're alone.

#  Never [[Answer the Door Safely|answer the door]] unless you are expecting someone and only when you make sure that it is that person. Peek out of the peephole or window (do not open the door) first before answering the door. The person at the door may be a stranger. Also ask the parents for a list of people they know, and ask to describe them on the piece of paper.

#  [[Entertain Kids When You Are Babysitting|Have a structured idea of what you're going to do]] while you're babysitting. Make puppets with the children out of paper bags and have coloring books they like and crayons with you. Play their favorite activity, and do whatever they ask you to do as long as they are safe. [[Stay Safe at Night|Being safe]] is the most important task you can do when you are babysitting. You must keep the child happy especially if it's young. The parents can insult you for making the child sad. It always helps if you stay in a positive, up-beat attitude when you are watching children.

#  Never leave them out of your sight!'''Keep the children you're watching in one area''', so that you can make sure everyone's safe. If there are older children you are watching, keep them limited to the house, or if you're outside, to the backyard. Smaller children should stay where you can see them at all times. All children should be kept as far away from a street as possible.

#  [[Put a Babysitting Charge to Sleep|Put the children to bed]] at the time the parent wants them in bed. Don't let them fall asleep early or stay up late. If they go to bed early, they may wake up later and not go back to sleep! Put the children to sleep like they are always put to bed. If one of the children cry, or throw a fit, try to give them their favorite cuddly toy, or sippy cup/bottle. Especially with slightly older children who want to stay up to carry on playing, make them aware of the fact that there will be no more playing or fun anyway if they try staying up on purpose for you will not join in nor give them their games. If the child still cries for no reason this probably is because the child is tired. He/She will eventually fall asleep. Throughout the night check up on the children however many times you think is necessary.

#  [[Clean Fast|Clean up]] before the parents get home and while the children are sleeping. Pick up toys and dishes. Make it look like you were never there and the parents will greatly appreciate it, because nobody wants to come home to a dirty home.

#  [[Play With Kids While Babysitting|Play with the kids]]! Kids love it when you play with them! Don't be afraid to go outside and get your hands dirty! Then fights and/or disagreements are less likely to pop up. Also the kids have an image of a fun, caring, trustworthy babysitter in their minds! Remember kids report how much they liked the babysitter and if they go on and on about how fun you were, you might get invited back! Just don't be afraid to let your inner child come out, the kids love it. Also don't forget that kids always love it when played with.
# Research ahead of time. What do the kids like? depending on their age, they will likely have different interests.
#  Become a certified babysitter. Look up classes to take. You will learn many new things and will be more trustworthy when it comes to babysitting an infant.

Then suggest that the children say something like Winnie The Pooh is going to take care of you, or something that sounds funny. Say, "Let's say it together." Say it with the child, then offer to check in their closet, under their bed, behind curtains, and any other place a monster may be hiding. added: *The kids you're babysitting won't fall asleep at the same time, so ask the ones who are not asleep to color with you (or find a quiet activity to engage in).

*To make the children behave more then make sticker chart before you arrive at the house. when you are at the house tell the children that when they get a certain amount of stars they will be rewarded with a biscuit or a sweet.
*If you're giving a child a bath, don't leave him/her alone for even two seconds. Make sure that you have all necessary bathing equipment in the bathroom before you put the child in the bathtub.

*A lot of children are scared of monsters at night. If you have trouble with the children, tell them, "I know a secret. It always works with me. It's a secret word that makes all monsters go away." Then suggest that the children say something like Winnie The Pooh is going to take care of you, or something that sounds funny. Say, "Let's say it together." Say it with the child, then offer to check in their closet, under their bed, behind curtains, and any other place a monster may be hiding. Be sure to tell the child before you leave that you've checked and there are no monsters in their room, but the secret word will make all monsters stay away for good now.
*If the child is known to move a lot then ask the parents to bring out a play-pen, If they don't have one then put all of the children into one room with the cot and put on an appropriate film.
*Be nice to the kids and don't get in their face, that will scare them away but if you are family the case may be different and they may know you enough to not be scared of you.
*Never invite your friends or anyone over without the parent's permission.

*When you are changing a baby's diaper on a changing table or counter, make sure that you have everything (baby wipes, diapers, baby powder, etc.) within reach so that you won't have to walk away to get anything. Don't leave the child for even a second, because in that second they could roll off of the table. Even if the table has sides, they could hurt themselves. So stay with the child the entire time, and get the child off of the table as soon as possible.
*You might want to take a class first because parents would rather hire someone who knows what they are doing. Even better, give the parents references when you first meet them.
*Always feel free to call the parents if you feel you need to. They will usually always leave a couple of phone numbers for you to call.

*Always change the toddler or infant's diaper when instructed to. If you are not given a specific time, change the diaper before naps and after. Most of the time you will know when it is time to change it, as it is very smelly.
*If you are babysitting an infant, only feed them things the size of their fist or smaller.

*When putting a baby to bed, '''do not''' lay it on its belly. Your baby can get Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS) if you do that. Do not prop a baby up with pillows, as these may cause it to suffocate.
*Be VERY careful around animals, no matter how nice they seem.
*Never let toddlers walk up or down stairs without you with them.
*Never fall asleep when babysitting. It's never a good idea to fall asleep on the job, especially if the kids that you're baby-sitting for could get into mischief and trouble.
*'''Always''' keep an eye on the children you are babysitting, because they might get hurt when you are not looking. Never let small children out of your sight.
*Don't let them jump on the furniture.

added: [[Image:65969524_07c888ab7a.jpg|200px|right]]Babysitting a young child, whether it is a sibling or the neighbor next door, requires some training, patience and understanding of how to calm a child/baby or help and comfort them in case of need of any help of a poopy diaper or a mess that the baby makes while eating. Also if the child might have allergies.
[[Category:Babysitting]]
== Steps ==

#[[Prepare for a Babysitting Job|Prepare for the job]]. Check your [[Keep a Calendar|calendar]] to make sure you are available when asked to babysit. This will help avoid the frustration of a last minute change of plans due to poor planning. Find out what time you will be needed, night or day, and again check to make sure you are available. If not, you can ask the person if you can babysit another time, or babysit another child. All of us can't babysit at the right time, whether you go to school, whether working, whether busy or you have a kid to take care of yourself.

#  Write down the following information: [[Call Someone on a Cell Phone|cell phone number]], the address and the phone number of the place where they will be, and the child's name, blood type, doctor's name, doctor's number, and allergies. These are very important in an emergency. You have to know these because you never know what will happen. You technically need most of the kid/baby's medical information. Also ask where the first aid things are kept.

#  Make sure they give you ''all'' of the [[Be Prepared for Any Kind of Emergency (for Kids)|emergency]] phone numbers needed. Police, ambulance, fire department and their cell phone numbers are very important, and should be written clearly on the refrigerator. If they give you a grandparent's phone number that’s also good, because the parents might be at a concert or somewhere loud and may not be able to hear their cell phone. Some other good people can be people the parents really know, and very good friends that you know well.

#  Make sure the parents give you instructions if caring for an [[Babysit an Infant|infant]]. Write down any and all instructions. It is better if the parents write it down because you could make a mistake when writing. This is yet another very important thing to do. Find out where all the gear, such as baby bottles or spare clothes, are kept.
#  Always make sure your the right age to do this big step. You should be '''at least''' 13  years old when you first start babysitting. Under that age, it might prove to be too much responsibility.
#  Ask in advance if you can do certain things such as cook, use the computer, use the TV, use the phone, etc. The parents may want to keep the lines clear in case they want to call.

#Make sure to find out any special household rules or off limits areas. Ask if they are expecting anyone or if you should [[Answer the Telephone When You're Babysitting|answer the phone]]. Better yet, let the answering machine take messages, this way you won't become nervous or distracted. You need to keep your eyes on the baby. No answering machine? Ask the parents to get one, or you can forward it to your cell phone so you can just grab it out of your pocket. Make sure the caller ID shows up, and don't pick up for a stranger. Ask the parents of phone numbers you can approve, and say that the parents aren't available, without telling them you're alone.

#  Never [[Answer the Door Safely|answer the door]] unless you are expecting someone and only when you make sure that it is that person. Peek out of the peephole or window (do not open the door) first before answering the door. The person at the door may be a stranger. Also ask the parents for a list of people they know, and ask to describe them on the piece of paper.

#  [[Entertain Kids When You Are Babysitting|Have a structured idea of what you're going to do]] while you're babysitting. Make puppets with the children out of paper bags and have coloring books they like and crayons with you. Play their favorite activity, and do whatever they ask you to do as long as they are safe. [[Stay Safe at Night|Being safe]] is the most important task you can do when you are babysitting. You must keep the child happy especially if it's young. The parents can insult you for making the child sad. It always helps if you stay in a positive, up-beat attitude when you are watching children.

#  Never leave them out of your sight!'''Keep the children you're watching in one area''', so that you can make sure everyone's safe. If there are older children you are watching, keep them limited to the house, or if you're outside, to the backyard. Smaller children should stay where you can see them at all times. All children should be kept as far away from a street as possible.

#  [[Put a Babysitting Charge to Sleep|Put the children to bed]] at the time the parent wants them in bed. Don't let them fall asleep early or stay up late. If they go to bed early, they may wake up later and not go back to sleep! Put the children to sleep like they are always put to bed. If one of the children cry, or throw a fit, try to give them their favortie cuddly toy, or sippy cup/bottle. Especially with slightly older children who want to stay up to carry on playing, make them aware of the fact that there will be no more playing or fun anyway if they try staying up on purpose for you will not join in nor give them their games. If the child still cries for no reason this probably is because the child is tired. He/She will eventually fall asleep. Throughout the night check up on the children however many times you think is necessary.

#  [[Clean Fast|Clean up]] before the parents get home and while the children are sleeping. Pick up toys and dishes. Make it look like you were never there and the parents will greatly appreciate it, because nobody wants to come home to a dirty home.

#  [[Play With Kids While Babysitting|Play with the kids]]! Kids love it when you play with them! Don't be afraid to go outside and get your hands dirty! Then fights and/or disagreements are less likely to pop up. Also the kids have an image of a fun, caring, trustworthy babysitter in their minds! Remember kids report how much they liked the babysitter and if they go on and on about how fun you were, you might get invited back! Just don't be afraid to let your inner child come out, the kids love it. Also don't forget that kids always love it when played with.
#  Become a certified babysitter. Look up classes to take. You will learn many new things and will be more trustworthy when it comes to babysitting an infant.

== Tips ==
*You might want to take a class first because parents would rather hire someone who knows what they are doing. Even better, give the parents references when you first meet them.

*Always change the toddler or infant's diaper when instructed to. If you are not given a specific time, change the diaper before naps and after. Most of the time you will know when it is time to change it, as it is very smelly.
*Be nice to the kids and don't get in their face, that will scare them away but if you are family the case may be different and they may know you enough to not be scared of you.

*When you are changing a baby's diaper on a changing table or counter, make sure that you have everything (baby wipes, diapers, baby powder, etc.) within reach so that you won't have to walk away to get anything. Don't leave the child for even a second, because in that second they could roll off of the table. Even if the table has sides, they could hurt themselves. So stay with the child the entire time, and get the child off of the table as soon as possible.

*A lot of children are scared of monsters at night. If you have trouble with the children, tell them, "I know a secret. It always works with me. It's a secret word that makes all monsters go away." Then suggest that the children say something like Winnie The Pooh is going to take care of you, or something that sounds funny. Say, "Let's say it together." Say it with the child, then offer to check in their closet, under their bed, behind curtains, and any other place a monster may be hiding. Be sure to tell the child before you leave that you've checked and there are no monsters in their room, but the secret word will make all monsters stay away for good now.
*Get a movie that you would like to see (make sure it's appropriate for the kids) and watch it when they fall asleep.
*Try to make the least amount of noise as possible so they won't wake up until their parents get home.
*The kids you're babysitting won't fall asleep at the same time, so ask the ones who are not asleep to color with you (or find a quiet activity to engage in).
*Find a cookbook and make no-bake cookies if you can't use the oven.Yum Yum
*If you are able to, keep the child's information so you don't have to write it down every time. Just make sure you don't forget it next time.
*If you're giving a child a bath, don't leave him/her alone for even two seconds. Make sure that you have all necessary bathing equipment in the bathroom before you put the child in the bathtub.
*If you are watching a young child, and there are dogs, keep the child away from the dog. If at all possible, keep the dog in a separate room or outside.
*If the child is known to move a lot then ask the parents to bring out a play-pen, If they don't have one then put all of the children into one room with the cot and put on an appropriate film.

*If the children will not go to sleep then put on a film that is appropriate(not a cartoon and not a musical)this will make them bored and make them sleep more,however,if that doesn't work then make them a hot drink but add cold water (1/3)this will also make them sleepy.

*To make the children behave more then make sticker chart before you arrive at the house. when you are at the house tell the children that when they get a certain amount of stars they will be rewarded with a biscuit or a sweet.
*Always feel free to call the parents if you feel you need to. They will usually always leave a couple of phone numbers for you to call.
*Never invite your friends or anyone over without the parent's permission.
== Warnings ==

*Kid-proof the areas you will be playing in. Make sure all electrical outlets are covered and put all sharp objects away. Make sure you do not let the kids get near cleaning fluids. Keep all types of medicines away, the child could think it is candy and gobble them up. Close all windows. If you're watching a toddler, keep all doors leading to basement stairs closed, and all bathroom doors closed.
*Don't let them jump on the furniture.
*Don't give kids anything packed with sugar even if they cry for it, unless the treat is approved by the parents.
*Follow the rules given to you by the parent. If you disobey them, they probably will not invite you back.

*When putting a baby to bed, '''do not''' lay it on its belly. Your baby can get Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS) if you do that. Do not prop a baby up with pillows, as these may cause it to suffocate.
*If you are babysitting an infant, only feed them things the size of their fist or smaller.
*Never fall asleep when babysitting. It's never a good idea to fall asleep on the job, especially if the kids that you're baby-sitting for could get into mischief and trouble.
*'''Always''' keep an eye on the children you are babysitting, because they might get hurt when you are not looking. Never let small children out of your sight.
*Never let toddlers walk up or down stairs without you with them.
*Be VERY careful around animals, no matter how nice they seem.
== Things You will Need ==
*Crafts
*Notepad for messages
*Bag or Tote
*Coloring pages
*Books
*Crayons/ Pencils/ Markers
*Games
*A fun and parent approved video for them to watch
*Emergency information
*Small snacks for you and the kids (Be cautious of any food allergies.)
*Clean diapers
*Page for scavenger hunt
*A pen to write the stuff with
*A booster seat if traveling (if they need it)
*A stroller (if going to walk around the park and are small children)
*Transport if you are taking to movies or into town
*Rewards for a good job (cookies or pencils will do)
*References (optional)
*First aid kit
*Cell phone (if you have one)
*Hand sanitizer
*Back up clothes

== Steps ==

#[[Prepare for a Babysitting Job|Prepare for the job]]. Check your [[Keep a Calendar|calendar]] to make sure you are available when asked to babysit. This will help avoid the frustration of a last minute change of plans due to poor planning. Find out what time you will be needed, night or day, and again check to make sure you are available. If not, you can ask the person if you can babysit another time, or babysit another child. All of us can't babysit at the right time, whether you go to school, whether working, whether busy or you have a kid to take care of yourself.

#  Write down the following information: [[Call Someone on a Cell Phone|cell phone number]], the address and the phone number of the place where they will be, and the child's name, blood type, doctor's name, doctor's number, and allergies. These are very important in an emergency. You have to know these because you never know what will happen. You technically need most of the kid/baby's medical information. Also ask where the first aid things are kept.

#  Make sure they give you ''all'' of the [[Be Prepared for Any Kind of Emergency (for Kids)|emergency]] phone numbers needed. Police, ambulance, fire department and their cell phone numbers are very important, and should be written clearly on the refrigerator. If they give you a grandparent's phone number that’s also good, because the parents might be at a concert or somewhere loud and may not be able to hear their cell phone. Some other good people can be people the parents really know, and very good friends that you know well.

#  Make sure the parents give you instructions if caring for an [[Babysit an Infant|infant]]. Write down any and all instructions. It is better if the parents write it down because you could make a mistake when writing. This is yet another very important thing to do. Find out where all the gear, such as baby bottles or spare clothes, are kept.
#  Always make sure your the right age to do this big step. You should be '''at least''' 13  years old when you first start babysitting. Under that age, it might prove to be too much responsibility.
#  Ask in advance if you can do certain things such as cook, use the computer, use the TV, use the phone, etc. The parents may want to keep the lines clear in case they want to call.

#Make sure to find out any special household rules or off limits areas. Ask if they are expecting anyone or if you should [[Answer the Telephone When You're Babysitting|answer the phone]]. Better yet, let the answering machine take messages, this way you won't become nervous or distracted. You need to keep your eyes on the baby. No answering machine? Ask the parents to get one, or you can forward it to your cell phone so you can just grab it out of your pocket. Make sure the caller ID shows up, and don't pick up for a stranger. Ask the parents of phone numbers you can approve, and say that the parents aren't available, without telling them you're alone.

#  Never [[Answer the Door Safely|answer the door]] unless you are expecting someone and only when you make sure that it is that person. Peek out of the peephole or window (do not open the door) first before answering the door. The person at the door may be a stranger. Also ask the parents for a list of people they know, and ask to describe them on the piece of paper.

#  [[Entertain Kids When You Are Babysitting|Have a structured idea of what you're going to do]] while you're babysitting. Make puppets with the children out of paper bags and have coloring books they like and crayons with you. Play their favorite activity, and do whatever they ask you to do as long as they are safe. [[Stay Safe at Night|Being safe]] is the most important task you can do when you are babysitting. You must keep the child happy especially if it's young. The parents can insult you for making the child sad. It always helps if you stay in a positive, up-beat attitude when you are watching children.

#  Never leave them out of your sight!'''Keep the children you're watching in one area''', so that you can make sure everyone's safe. If there are older children you are watching, keep them limited to the house, or if you're outside, to the backyard. Smaller children should stay where you can see them at all times. All children should be kept as far away from a street as possible.

#  [[Put a Babysitting Charge to Sleep|Put the children to bed]] at the time the parent wants them in bed. Don't let them fall asleep early or stay up late. If they go to bed early, they may wake up later and not go back to sleep! Put the children to sleep like they are always put to bed. If one of the children cry, or throw a fit, try to give them their favortie cuddly toy, or sippy cup/bottle. Especially with slightly older children who want to stay up to carry on playing, make them aware of the fact that there will be no more playing or fun anyway if they try staying up on purpose for you will not join in nor give them their games. If the child still cries for no reason this probably is because the child is tired. He/She will eventually fall asleep. Throughout the night check up on the children however many times you think is necessary.

#  [[Clean Fast|Clean up]] before the parents get home and while the children are sleeping. Pick up toys and dishes. Make it look like you were never there and the parents will greatly appreciate it, because nobody wants to come home to a dirty home.

#  [[Play With Kids While Babysitting|Play with the kids]]! Kids love it when you play with them! Don't be afraid to go outside and get your hands dirty! Then fights and/or disagreements are less likely to pop up. Also the kids have an image of a fun, caring, trustworthy babysitter in their minds! Remember kids report how much they liked the babysitter and if they go on and on about how fun you were, you might get invited back! Just don't be afraid to let your inner child come out, the kids love it. Also don't forget that kids always love it when played with.
#  Become a certified babysitter. Look up classes to take. You will learn many new things and will be more trustworthy when it comes to babysitting an infant.
== Video ==
{{Video:Babysit|}}
== Tips ==
*You might want to take a class first because parents would rather hire someone who knows what they are doing. Even better, give the parents references when you first meet them.

*Always change the toddler or infant's diaper when instructed to. If you are not given a specific time, change the diaper before naps and after. Most of the time you will know when it is time to change it, as it is very smelly.
*Be nice to the kids and don't get in their face, that will scare them away but if you are family the case may be different and they may know you enough to not be scared of you.

*When you are changing a baby's diaper on a changing table or counter, make sure that you have everything (baby wipes, diapers, baby powder, etc.) within reach so that you won't have to walk away to get anything. Don't leave the child for even a second, because in that second they could roll off of the table. Even if the table has sides, they could hurt themselves. So stay with the child the entire time, and get the child off of the table as soon as possible.

*A lot of children are scared of monsters at night. If you have trouble with the children, tell them, "I know a secret. It always works with me. It's a secret word that makes all monsters go away." Then suggest that the children say something like Winnie The Pooh is going to take care of you, or something that sounds funny. Say, "Let's say it together." Say it with the child, then offer to check in their closet, under their bed, behind curtains, and any other place a monster may be hiding. Be sure to tell the child before you leave that you've checked and there are no monsters in their room, but the secret word will make all monsters stay away for good now.
*Get a movie that you would like to see (make sure it's appropriate for the kids) and watch it when they fall asleep.
*Try to make the least amount of noise as possible so they won't wake up until their parents get home.
*The kids you're babysitting won't fall asleep at the same time, so ask the ones who are not asleep to color with you (or find a quiet activity to engage in).
*Find a cookbook and make no-bake cookies if you can't use the oven.Yum Yum
*If you are able to, keep the child's information so you don't have to write it down every time. Just make sure you don't forget it next time.
*If you're giving a child a bath, don't leave him/her alone for even two seconds. Make sure that you have all necessary bathing equipment in the bathroom before you put the child in the bathtub.
*If you are watching a young child, and there are dogs, keep the child away from the dog. If at all possible, keep the dog in a separate room or outside.
*If the child is known to move a lot then ask the parents to bring out a play-pen, If they don't have one then put all of the children into one room with the cot and put on an appropriate film.

*If the children will not go to sleep then put on a film that is appropriate(not a cartoon and not a musical)this will make them bored and make them sleep more,however,if that doesn't work then make them a hot drink but add cold water (1/3)this will also make them sleepy.

*To make the children behave more then make sticker chart before you arrive at the house. when you are at the house tell the children that when they get a certain amount of stars they will be rewarded with a biscuit or a sweet.
*Always feel free to call the parents if you feel you need to. They will usually always leave a couple of phone numbers for you to call.
*Never invite your friends or anyone over without the parent's permission.
== Warnings ==

*Kid-proof the areas you will be playing in. Make sure all electrical outlets are covered and put all sharp objects away. Make sure you do not let the kids get near cleaning fluids. Keep all types of medicines away, the child could think it is candy and gobble them up. Close all windows. If you're watching a toddler, keep all doors leading to basement stairs closed, and all bathroom doors closed.
*Don't let them jump on the furniture.
*Don't give kids anything packed with sugar even if they cry for it, unless the treat is approved by the parents.
*Follow the rules given to you by the parent. If you disobey them, they probably will not invite you back.

*When putting a baby to bed, '''do not''' lay it on its belly. Your baby can get Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS) if you do that. Do not prop a baby up with pillows, as these may cause it to suffocate.
*If you are babysitting an infant, only feed them things the size of their fist or smaller.
*Never fall asleep when babysitting. It's never a good idea to fall asleep on the job, especially if the kids that you're baby-sitting for could get into mischief and trouble.
*'''Always''' keep an eye on the children you are babysitting, because they might get hurt when you are not looking. Never let small children out of your sight.
*Never let toddlers walk up or down stairs without you with them.
*Be VERY careful around animals, no matter how nice they seem.
== Things You will Need ==
*Crafts
*Notepad for messages
*Bag or Tote
*Coloring pages
*Books
*Crayons/ Pencils/ Markers
*Games
*A fun and parent approved video for them to watch
*Emergency information
*Small snacks for you and the kids (Be cautious of any food allergies.)
*Clean diapers
*Page for scavenger hunt
*A pen to write the stuff with
*A booster seat if traveling (if they need it)
*A stroller (if going to walk around the park and are small children)
*Transport if you are taking to movies or into town
*Rewards for a good job (cookies or pencils will do)
*References (optional)
*First aid kit
*Cell phone (if you have one)
*Hand sanitizer
*Back up clothes
