added: #'''[[Entertain Kids When You Are Babysitting|Have a structured idea of what you're going to do]] while you're babysitting.''' Make puppets with the children out of paper bags and have coloring books they like and crayons with you. Play their favorite activity, and do whatever they ask you to do as long as they are safe. [[Stay Safe at Night|Being safe]] is the most important task you can do when you are babysitting. You must keep the child happy especially if its young. The parents can insult you for making the child sad. It always helps if you stay in a positive, up-beat attitude when you are watching children.

#'''[[Put a Babysitting Charge to Sleep|Put the children to bed]] at the time the parent wants them in bed.''' Don't let them fall asleep early or stay up late. If they go to bed early, they may wake up later and not go back to sleep! Put the children to sleep like they are always put to bed. If one of the children cry, or throw a fit, try to give them their favortie toy, or sippy cup/bottle. If the child still cries for no reason this probably is because the child is tired. He/She will eventually fall asleep. Throughout the night check up on the children however many time you think is necessary.

#'''[[Clean Fast|Clean up]] before the parents get home''' and while the children are sleeping. Pick up toys and dishes. Make it look like you were never there and the parents will greatly appreciate it, becaus nocody want to come home to a dirty home.
*Always feel free to call the parents if you feel you need to. They will usually always leave a couple of phone numbers for you to call.

*Kid-proof the areas you will be playing in. Make sure all electrical outlets are covered and put all sharp objects away. Make sure you do not let the kids get near cleaning fluids. Keep all types of medicines away, the child could think it is candy and gobble them up. Close all windows. If you're watching a toddler, keep all doors leading to basement stairs closed, and all bathroom doors closed.

added: == Steps ==

#'''[[Prepare for a Babysitting Job|Prepare for the job]].''' Check your [[Keep a Calendar|calendar]] to make sure you are available when asked to babysit. This will help avoid the frustration of a last minute change of plans due to poor planning. Find out what time you will be needed, night or day, and again check to make sure you are available. If not, you can ask the person if you can babysit another time, or babysit another child. All of us can't babysit at the right time, whether you go to school, whether working, whether busy or you have a kid to take care of yourself.

#'''Write down the following information:''' [[Call Someone on a Cell Phone|cell phone number]], the address and the phone number of the place where they will be, and the child's name, blood type, doctor's name, doctor's number, and allergies. These are very important in an emergency. You have to know these because you never know what will happen. You technically need most of the kid/baby's medical information. Also ask where the first aid things are kept.

#'''Make sure they give you ''all'' of the [[Be Prepared for Any Kind of Emergency (for Kids)|emergency]] phone numbers needed.''' Police, ambulance, and their cell phone numbers are very important, and should be written clearly on the refrigerator. If they give you a grandparent's phone number that’s also good, because the parents might be at a concert or somewhere loud and may not be able to hear their cell phone. Some other good people can be people the parents really know, and very good friends that you know well.

#'''Make sure the parents give you instructions if caring for an [[Babysit an Infant|infant]].''' Write down any and all instructions. It is better if the parents write it down because you could make a mistake when writing. This is yet another very important thing to do. Find out where all the gear, such as baby bottles or spare clothes, are kept.
#'''Ask in advance if you can do certain things''' such as cook, use the computer, use the TV, use the phone, etc. The parents may want to keep the lines clear in case they want to call.

#'''Make sure to find out any special household rules or off limits areas.''' Ask if they are expecting anyone or if you should [[Answer the Telephone When You're Babysitting|answer the phone]]. Better yet, let the answering machine take messages, this way you won't become nervous or distracted. You need to keep your eyes on the baby. No answering machine? Ask the parents to get one, or you can forward it to your cellphone so you can just grab it out of your pocket. Make sure the caller ID shows up, and don't pick up for a stranger. Ask the parents of phone numbers you can approve, and say that the parents aren't available, without telling them you're alone.

#'''Never [[Answer the Door Safely|answer the door]] unless you are expecting someone''' and only when you make sure that it is that person. Peek out of the peephole or window (do not open the door) first before answering the door. The person at the door may be a stranger. Also ask the parents for a list of people they know, and ask to describe them on the piece of paper.

#'''[[Entertain Kids When You Are Babysitting|Have a structured idea of what you're going to do]] while you're babysitting.''' Make puppets with the children out of paper bags and have coloring books they like and crayons with you. Play their favorite activity, and do whatever they ask you to do as long as they are safe. You must keep the child happy especially if its young. The parents can insult you for making the child sad.

Never leave them out of your sight!]]'''Keep the children you're watching in one area''', so that you can make sure everyone's safe. If there are older children you are watching, keep them limited to the house, or if you're outside, to the backyard. Smaller children should stay where you can see them at all times. All children should be kept as far away from a street as possible.

#'''[[Put a Babysitting Charge to Sleep|Put the children to bed]] at the time the parent wants them in bed.''' Don't let them fall asleep early or stay up late. If they go to bed early, they may wake up later and not go back to sleep!

#'''[[Clean Fast|Clean up]] before the parents get home''' and while the children are sleeping. Pick up toys and dishes. Make it look like you were never there and the parents will greatly appreciate it.

*Always change the toddler or infant's diaper when instructed to. If you are not given a specific time, change the diaper before naps and after. Most of the time you will know when it is time to change it, as it is very stinky.

*When you are changing a baby's diaper on a changing table or counter, make sure that you have everything (baby wipes, diapers, baby powder, etc.) within reach so that you won't have to walk away to get anything. Don't leave the child for even a second, because in that second they could roll off of the table. Even if the table has sides, they could hurt themselves. So stay with the child the entire time, and get the child off of the table as soon as possible.

*A lot of children are scared of monsters at night. If you have trouble with the children, tell them, "I know a secret. It always works with me. It's a secret word that makes all monsters go away." Then suggest that the children say something like Pooh Pa Ja, or something that sounds funny. Say, "Let's say it together." Say it with the child, then offer to check in their closet, under their bed, behind curtains, and any other place a monster may be hiding. Be sure to tell the child before you leave that you've checked and there are no monsters in their room, but the secret word will make all monsters stay away for good now.
*Get a movie that you would like to see (make sure it's appropriate for the kids) and watch it when they fall asleep.
*Try to make the least amount of noise as possible so they won't wake up until their parents get home.
*The kids you're babysitting won't fall asleep at the same time, so ask the ones who are not asleep to color with you (or find a quiet activity to engage in).
*Find a cookbook and make no-bake cookies if you can't use the oven.
*If you are able to, keep the child's information so you don't have to write it down every time. Just make sure you don't forget it next time.
*If you're giving a child a bath, don't leave him/her alone for even two seconds. Make sure that you have all necessary bathing equipment in the bathroom before you put the child in the bathtub.
*If you are watching a young child, and there are dogs, keep the child away from the dog. If at all possible, keep the dog in a separate room or outside.

*Kid-proof the areas you will be playing in. Make sure all electrical outlets are covered and put all sharp objects away. Make sure you do not let the kids get near cleaning fluids. Close all windows. If you're watching a toddler, keep all doors leading to basement stairs closed, and all bathroom doors closed.
*Don't let them jump on the furniture.
*Don't give kids anything packed with sugar even if they cry for it, unless the treat is approved by the parents.
*Follow the rules given to you by the parent. If you disobey them, they probably will not invite you back.
*When putting a baby to bed, '''do not''' lay it on its belly. Your baby can get Sudden Infant Death Syndrome if you do that. Do not prop a baby up with pillows, as these may cause it to suffocate.
*If you are babysitting an infant, never give them anything the size of their fist or smaller.
*Never fall asleep when babysitting. It's never a good idea to fall asleep on the job, especially if the kids that your baby-sitting for could get into mischief and trouble.

added: #'''[[Prepare for a Babysitting Job|Prepare for the job]].''' Check your [[Keep a Calendar|calendar]] to make sure you are available when asked to babysit. This will help avoid the frustration of a last minute change of plans due to poor planning. Find out what time you will be needed, night or day, and again check to make sure you are available. If not, you can ask the person if you can babysit another time, or babysit another child. All of us can't babysit at the right time, whether you go to school, whether working, whether busy or you have a kid to take care of yourself.

#'''Write down the following information:''' [[Call Someone on a Cell Phone|cell phone number]], the address and the phone number of the place where they will be, and the child's name, blood type, doctor's name, doctor's number, and allergies. These are very important in an emergency. You have to know these because you never know what will happen. You technically need most of the kid/baby's medical information.  Also ask where the first aid things are kept.

#'''Make sure they give you ''all'' of the [[Be Prepared for Any Kind of Emergency (for Kids)|emergency]] phone numbers needed.''' Police, ambulance, and their cell phone numbers are very important, and should be written clearly on the refrigerator. If they give you a grandparent's phone number that’s also good, because the parents might be at a concert or somewhere loud and may not be able to hear their cell phone. Some other good people can be people the parents really know, and very good friends that you know well.

#'''Make sure the parents give you instructions if caring for an [[Babysit an Infant|infant]].''' Write down any and all instructions. It is better if the parents write it down because you could make a mistake when writing. This is yet another very important thing to do. Find out where all the gear, such as baby bottles or spare clothes, are kept.
#'''Ask in advance if you can do certain things''' such as cook, use the computer, use the TV, use the phone, etc. The parents may want to keep the lines clear in case they want to call.

#'''Make sure to find out any special household rules or off limits areas.''' Ask if they are expecting anyone or if you should [[Answer the Telephone When You're Babysitting|answer the phone]]. Better yet, let the answering machine take messages, this way you won't become nervous or distracted. You need to keep your eyes on the baby. No answering machine? Ask the parents to get one, or you can forward it to your cellphone so you can just grab it out of your pocket. Make sure the caller ID shows up, and don't pick up for a stranger. Ask the parents of phone numbers you can approve, and say that the parents aren't available, without telling them you're alone.

#'''Never [[Answer the Door Safely|answer the door]] unless you are expecting someone''' and only when you make sure that it is that person. Peek out of the peephole or window (do not open the door) first before answering the door. The person at the door may be a stranger. Also ask the parents for a list of people they know, and ask to describe them on the piece of paper.

#'''[[Entertain Kids When You Are Babysitting|Have a structured idea of what you're going to do]] while you're babysitting.''' Make puppets with the children out of paper bags and have coloring books they like and crayons with you. Play their favorite activity, and do whatever they ask you to do as long as they are safe. You must keep the child happy especially if its young. The parents can insult you for making the child sad.

#[[Image:0721071639.jpg 226.jpg|thumb|Never leave them out of your sight!]]'''Keep the children you're watching in one area''', so that you can make sure everyone's safe. If there are older children you are watching, keep them limited to the house, or if you're outside, to the backyard. Smaller children should stay where you can see them at all times. All children should be kept as far away from a street as possible.

#'''[[Put a Babysitting Charge to Sleep|Put the children to bed]] at the time the parent wants them in bed.''' Don't let them fall asleep early or stay up late. If they go to bed early, they may wake up later and not go back to sleep!

#'''[[Clean Fast|Clean up]] before the parents get home''' and while the children are sleeping. Pick up toys and dishes. Make it look like you were never there and the parents will greatly appreciate it.

*Kid-proof the areas you will be playing in. Make sure all electrical outlets are covered and put all sharp objects away.  Make sure you do not let the kids get near cleaning fluids. *When putting a baby to bed, '''do not''' lay it on its belly. Your baby can get Sudden Infant Death Syndrome if you do that. Do not prop a baby up with pillows, as these may cause it to suffocate.

*When you are changing a baby's diaper on a changing table or counter, make sure that you have everything (baby wipes, diapers, baby powder, etc.) within reach so that you won't have to walk away to get anything. Don't leave the child for even a second, because in that second they could roll off of the table. Even if the table has sides, they could hurt themselves. So stay with the child the entire time, and get the child off of the table as soon as possible.

*A lot of children are scared of monsters at night. If you have trouble with the children, tell them, "I know a secret. It always works with me. It's a secret word that makes all monsters go away." Then suggest that the children say something like Pooh Pa Ja, or something that sounds funny. Say, "Let's say it together." Say it with the child, then offer to check in their closet, under their bed, behind curtains, and any other place a monster may be hiding. Be sure to tell the child before you leave that you've checked and there are no monsters in their room, but the secret word will make all monsters stay away for good now.
*Get a movie that you would like to see (make sure it's appropriate for the kids) and watch it when they fall asleep.
*The kids you're babysitting won't fall asleep at the same time, so ask the ones who are not asleep to color with you (or find a quiet activity to engage in).
*Find a cookbook and make no-bake cookies if you can't use the oven.
*If you're giving a child a bath, don't leave him/her alone for even two seconds. Make sure that you have all necessary bathing equipment in the bathroom before you put the child in the bathtub.
*If you are watching a young child, and there are dogs, keep the child away from the dog. If at all possible, keep the dog in a separate room or outside.

*Make sure all electrical outlets are covered and put all sharp objects away.  Make sure you do not let the kids get near cleaning fluids. Close all windows. If you're watching a toddler, keep all doors leading to basement stairs closed, and all bathroom doors closed.

*If you are babysitting an infant, never give them anything the size of their fist or smaller.

*Never leave the house unless you asked.

removed: #Bring a notepad so you are able to take messages if someone calls and so you can write down all important information about the child in case of an emergency. Also, write down the parent's cell phone number, the address and the phone number of the place where they will be, and the child's name, blood type, doctor's name, doctor's number, and allergies. These are very important in an emergency. You have to know these because you never know what will happen. You technically need most of the kid/baby's medical information. This is very important.

#Next, before they leave the house, make sure they give you ''all'' of the emergency phone numbers needed. Police, ambulance, and their cell phone numbers are very important, and should be written clearly on the refrigerator. If they give you a grandparent's phone number that’s also good, because the parents might be at a concert or somewhere loud and may not be able to hear their cell phone. Some other good people can be people the parents really know, and very good friends that you know well. Young people are better than senior citizens, but the thing is that young people probably wouldn't know well and the old people have the experience and wisdom, but young people are fast, and strong and old people are slow and weak. Your best bet will probably be middle-aged people.

#Make sure you also have their address written clearly in case of an emergency, so you will know exactly where you are, even if you are just five houses from your own home. This is another thing important, and remember, you need most of the information. Even if you are across the street or the house next to it you need to know all the info in case of a huge emergency.

# Make sure the parents give you some baby bottles or instructions for what to do if the baby wakes up, when babysitting an infant, Write down any and all instructions. It is better if the parents write it down because you could make a mistake when writing. This is yet another very important thing to do. If you put the baby to sleep on its belly, it may die. So that is why this is so important. Your baby can get Sudden Infant Death Syndrome if you do that.

#Let the answering machine take messages, this way you won't become nervous or distracted. You need to keep your eyes on the baby. No answering machine? Ask the parents to get one, or you can forward it to your cellphone so you can just grab it out of your pocket. Make sure the caller ID shows up, and don't pick up for a stranger. Ask the parents of phone numbers you can approve, and say that the parents aren't available, without telling them you're alone.

#''Never'' answer the door unless you are expecting someone and ''only''when you make sure that it is ''that'' person. Peek out of the peephole or window (do not open the door!) first before answering the door. The person at the door may be a stranger. Also ask the parents for a list of people they know, and ask to describe on the piece of paper.

# Have a structured idea of what you're going to do while you're babysitting. Make puppets with the children out of paper bags and have coloring books they like and crayons with you. Play their favorite activity, and do whatever they ask you to do as long as they are safe. You must keep the child happy especially if its young. The parents can insult you for making the child sad.
#Make sure to find out any special household rules or off limits areas.
#Ask if they are expecting anyone or if you should answer the phone.

added: [[Image:65969524_07c888ab7a.jpg|200px|right]]Babysitting a young child, whether it is a sibling or the neighbor next door, requires some training, patience and understanding of how to calm a child or help and comfort them in case of need.

# Check your calendar to make sure you are available when asked to babysit. This will help avoid the frustration of a last minute change of plans due to poor planning. Find out what time you will be needed, night or day, and again check to make sure you are available. If not, you can ask the person if you can babysit another time, or babysit another child. All of us can't babysit at the right time, whether you go to school, whether working, whether busy or you have a kid to take care of yourself.

#Bring a notepad so you are able to take messages if someone calls and so you can write down all important information about the child in case of an emergency. Also, write down the parent's cell phone number, the address and the phone number of the place where they will be, and the child's name, blood type, doctor's name, doctor's number, and allergies. These are very important in an emergency. You have to know these because you never know what will happen. You technically need most of the kid/baby's medical information. This is very important.

#Next, before they leave the house, make sure they give you ''all'' of the emergency phone numbers needed. Police, ambulance, and their cell phone numbers are very important, and should be written clearly on the refrigerator. If they give you a grandparent's phone number that’s also good, because the parents might be at a concert or somewhere loud and may not be able to hear their cell phone. Some other good people can be people the parents really know, and very good friends that you know well. Young people are better than senior citizens, but the thing is that young people probably wouldn't know well and the old people have the experience and wisdom, but young people are fast, and strong and old people are slow and weak. Your best bet will probably be middle-aged people.

#Make sure you also have their address written clearly in case of an emergency, so you will know exactly where you are, even if you are just five houses from your own home. This is another thing important, and remember, you need most of the information. Even if you are across the street or the house next to it you need to know all the info in case of a huge emergency.

# Make sure the parents give you some baby bottles or instructions for what to do if the baby wakes up, when babysitting an infant, Write down any and all instructions. It is better if the parents write it down because you could make a mistake when writing. This is yet another very important thing to do. If you put the baby to sleep on its belly, it may die. So that is why this is so important. Your baby can get Sudden Infant Death Syndrome if you do that.

#Let the answering machine take messages, this way you won't become nervous or distracted. You need to keep your eyes on the baby. No answering machine? Ask the parents to get one, or you can forward it to your cellphone so you can just grab it out of your pocket. Make sure the caller ID shows up, and don't pick up for a stranger. Ask the parents of phone numbers you can approve, and say that the parents aren't available, without telling them you're alone.

#''Never'' answer the door unless you are expecting someone and ''only''when you make sure that it is ''that'' person. Peek out of the peephole or window (do not open the door!) first before answering the door. The person at the door may be a stranger. Also ask the parents for a list of people they know, and ask to describe on the piece of paper.

# Have a structured idea of what you're going to do while you're babysitting. Make puppets with the children out of paper bags and have coloring books they like and crayons with you. Play their favorite activity, and do whatever they ask you to do as long as they are safe. You must keep the child happy especially if its young. The parents can insult you for making the child sad.
#Make sure to find out any special household rules or off limits areas.
#Ask if they are expecting anyone or if you should answer the phone.
== Tips ==

*Always change the toddler or infant's diaper when instructed to. If you are not given a specific time, change the diaper before naps and after. Most of the time you will know when it is time to change it, as it is very smelly.
*Don't use the phone unless it is absolutely necessary.
*Put the child to bed at the time the parent wants them in bed. Don't let them fall asleep early or stay up late. If they go to bed early, they may wake up later and not go back to sleep!

*Keep them occupied. If the 3-year-old scribbles on the wall chances are you won't be invited back. You can fix any mistakes if you need to stay, like washing it off. But be sure to keep your eyes on the kid the whole time, and keep dangerous things away from it like toxic crayons, and matches etc.
*Answer the phone politely and take detailed messages.
*Always leave the house tidy.
*Follow the rules that the parents leave.
*Always be polite.
*Don't give kids anything packed with sugar even if they cry for it, unless the treat is approved by the parents.
*Get a movie that you would like to see (make sure it's appropriate for the kids)and watch it when they fall asleep.
*Try to make the least amount of noise as possible so they won't wake up until their parents get home.
*Bring money just in case of an emergency.
*The kids you're babysitting won't fall asleep at the same time, so ask the ones who are not asleep to color with you (or find a quiet activity to engage in).
**Find a cookbook and make no-bake cookies if you can't use the oven.
*If you are able to, keep the child's information so you don't have to write it down every time. Just make sure you don't forget it next time.
*Do not use the Internet unless you ask the parents and they say yes.
*Never leave the house unless you asked.
*Never fall asleep when babysitting.
*If two kids are fighting don't just sit there and watch.
== Warnings ==
*Make sure all electrical outlets are covered.
*Put all sharp objects away.
*Don't let them jump on the furniture.
*Close all windows.
*Follow the rules given to you by the parent. If you disobey them, they probably will not invite you back.
*Make sure you do not let the kids get near cleaners.
*When putting a baby to bed, '''DO NOT''' lay it on its belly. DO NOT prop a baby up with pillows, as these may cause it to suffocate.
*if you are babysitting an infant, never give them anything the size of their fist or smaller
== Things You'll Need ==
*Crafts
*Notepad for messages.
*Bag or Tote
*Cell Phone
*Money
*Coloring pages
*Entertainment
*A fun and parent approved video for them to watch (if they are good)
*  emergency information

added: # Check your calendar to make sure you are available when asked to babysit. This will help avoid the frustration of a last minute change of plans due to poor planning. Find out what time you will be needed, night or day, and again check to make sure you are available. If not, you can ask the person if you can babysit another time, or babysit another child. All of us can't babysit at the right time, whether you go to school, whether working, whether busy or you have a kid to take care of yourself.

#Bring a notepad so you are able to take messages if someone calls and so you can write down all important information about the child in case of an emergency. Also, write down the parent's cell phone number, the address and the phone number of the place where they will be, and the child's name, blood type, doctor's name, doctor's number, and allergies. These are very important in an emergency. You have to know these because you never know what will happen. You technically need most of the kid/baby's medical information. This is very important.

#''Never'' answer the door unless you are expecting someone and ''only''when you make sure that it is ''that'' person. Peek out of the peephole or window (do not open the door!) first before answering the door. The person at the door may be a stranger. Also ask the parents for a list of people they know, and ask to describe on the piece of paper.

# Have a structured idea of what you're going to do while you're babysitting. Make puppets with the children out of paper bags and have coloring books they like and crayons with you. Play their favorite activity, and do whatever they ask you to do as long as they are safe. You must keep the child happy especially if its young. The parents can insult you for making the child sad.
*Put the child to bed at the time the parent wants them in bed. Don't let them fall asleep early or stay up late. If they go to bed early, they may wake up later and not go back to sleep!

*Keep them occupied. If the 3-year-old scribbles on the wall chances are you won't be invited back. You can fix any mistakes if you need to stay, like washing it off. But be sure to keep your eyes on the kid the whole time, and keep dangerous things away from it like toxic crayons, and matches etc.
*Answer the phone politely and take detailed messages.
*Follow the rules that the parents leave.
*If you are able to, keep the child's information so you don't have to write it down every time. Just make sure you don't forget it next time.
*Follow the rules given to you by the parent. If you disobey them, they probably will not invite you back.

added: == Tips ==

*Always change the toddler or infant's diaper when instructed to. If you are not given a specific time, change the diaper before naps and after. Most of the time you will know when it is time to change it, as it is very smelly.
*Put the child to bed at the time the parent wants them in bed.  Don't let them fall asleep early or stay up late.  If they go to bed early, they may wake up later and not go back to sleep!

*Keep them occupied.  If the 3-year-old scribbles on the wall chances are you won't be invited back. You can fix any mistakes if you need to stay, like washing it off. But be sure to keep your eyes on the kid the whole time, and keep dangerous things away from it like toxic crayons, and matches etc.
*Answer the phone politely and take  detailed messages.
*Always leave the house tidy.
*Follow  the rules that the parents leave.
*Always be polite.
*Don't give kids anything packed with sugar even if they cry for it.
*Get a movie that you would like to see (make sure it's appropriate for the kids)and watch it when they fall asleep.
*Try to make the least amount of noise as possible so they won't wake up until their parents get home.
*Bring money just in case of an emergency, or in case you don't have the movie they want to watch.

*The kids you're babysitting won't fall asleep at the same time, so ask the ones who are not asleep to color with you. Of course you can't leave the sleeping ones alone, so put the coloring books on the floor and color in the living room.
*Find a cookbook and make no-bake cookies or brownies if you can't use the oven.
*If you are able to, keep the child's information so you don't have to write it down every time.  Just make sure you don't forget it next time.
*Do not use the Internet unless you ask the parents and they say yes.
*Never leave the house unless you asked.
*Never fall aslep when babysitting.

*Always be polite to kids and parents!
*Don't give kids anything packed with sugar even if they cry for it.
